subject: Clarify: no-training pledge, ephemeral caches, and deletion timelines

Subject: Quick question about Redwood's 'no training' pledge and retention windows

Hi Alex,

We're progressing through procurement and I have a couple of targeted questions for our privacy team while we review the DPA:

1) The vendor questionnaire we received has the checkbox 'we do not train our models on customer-provided data.' Can you confirm in plain language whether Redwood uses any customer inputs (API payloads, uploaded files, embeddings, conversation logs) to update or fine-tune your production models?

2) If the answer to (1) is 'no', can you also explain what telemetry, logs, or aggregated signals (if any) you keep for product/quality improvements and the retention windows for each category (request logs, KV cache, embeddings, backups, audit logs)?

3) Finally, in the event we request deletion for a tenant, what are the timelines and scope (are backups scrubbed, do deletes remove embeddings, caches, derivative vectors)?

Appreciate a concise write-up I can attach to the RFP. If it's easier, happy to take a 30-minute call.

Thanks,
Jamie
Privacy Manager, Acme Corp

Hi Jamie,

Thanks for the clear questions — happy to clarify. Short answers up front, followed by details:

- Short answer on training: Redwood does not use customer-provided content to train or fine-tune our public models by default.
- Telemetry/retention: we retain certain operational logs for debugging and billing; KV caches are ephemeral and embeddings/logs retention depends on deployment mode (hosted vs Dedicated/Private).
- Deletion timelines: for hosted API customers who opt into standard settings, we complete deletions within 30 days for active indices and caches; longer windows apply for backups and forensic logs (see below). Dedicated and Private customers can negotiate different retention in contract.

I'm looping in Stephanie (Security & Compliance) to add the technical specifics and confirm the language you can include in the RFP/DPA. Michael from Sales is on copy for procurement context.

Would you like us to provide a formal statement you can attach to the RFP and a redlined DPA?

Best,
Alex Martinez

Hi all — thanks for the question, Jamie. Below is a concise, copy-ready explanation you can include in the RFP and share with your legal team. I've also attached a redline of our standard DPA showing the contractual commitments we typically offer.

Copy-ready statement (short):
Redwood Inference does not use customer-provided content (API payloads, uploaded files, embeddings, customer conversation logs) to train or fine-tune our public models. For hosted customers, customer data is processed to generate the requested inference only; we do not add customer content to model training datasets unless explicit, documented opt-in is granted by the customer via a formal program.

Operational telemetry and retention (by artifact):
- Request metadata (timestamps, request size, model variant): retained 90 days for billing and abuse detection, then deleted.
- Full request/response payloads (text, files, embeddings): default hosted retention = retained up to 30 days for troubleshooting; can be configured to 0 days for customers with stricter requirements or set via contract for Dedicated customers.
- KV cache / ephemeral session caches: TTL default = 1 hour; cache contents are not persisted to training datasets.
- Embeddings and derivative vectors: treated as customer data. Default hosted window is 30 days; Dedicated contracts may specify longer/shorter windows. On deletion request, embeddings are removed from active indices within 48 hours and purged from backups in the timeframe below.
- Audit logs (security/audit trails): retained 365 days for compliance; access is restricted and logs do not feed model training pipelines.
- Backups and snapshots: rolling backups retained up to 90 days by default; deletion requests are processed against active indexes immediately and against backups during the next backup rotation. For customers with contractually required shorter windows, we accommodate via Dedicated or Private deployment options.

What 'we do not train on your data' means (nuances):
1) Public model training: we do not add customer-provided content to the corpora or datasets used to train or fine-tune Redwood's public or upstream models without an explicit, written opt-in.
2) Product quality signals: we may collect aggregated, de-identified metrics (e.g., feature usage, latency histograms, aggregated error rates) to improve platform reliability. These metrics are not reversible to customer content and do not contain raw prompt/response text.
3) Opt-out and contract controls: customers can contractually opt out of any telemetry collection that could be used for model improvement. For regulated customers we offer Dedicated and Private deployment models where telemetry is limited per contractual terms or turned off entirely if deployed on-prem.

Deletion and verified purge process:
- Hosted (standard): active data removed from live indices/caches within 48 hours of verified request; we mark and schedule backup purges and complete backup deletion within 30 days.
- Backups/forensics: archived backups are rotated on a 90-day schedule by default; we flag backup sets for expedited purge where contractually required (expedited purge SLA negotiable).
- Verification: upon completion we provide a certificate of deletion with the identifiers purged and the timestamp.

Exceptions and law enforcement: we will not use or disclose customer data for training, except where compelled by valid legal process; we notify customers as permitted by law and per DPA.

Attachments: redline_dpa_v2.docx (contains example clause language to add to Section 4: Data Use & Model Training).

If you'd like, we can produce a one-page attestation on company letterhead and route it through Legal for signature.

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
